criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Frames 1, 5, 7 and 9 are strong physical scenes. Each has a weathering steel stair on dark caliche under a low key, with contact shadows and a lit pier. On frame 1 the missing middle treads read at feed size before a word is read. Frame 9 has a person for scale at the broken flight. Frame 2's txbench relief has real height, 6 materials and cast shadows. Weaker frames: frame 4 is three large flat beige pier faces filling the lower 60% in the grey middle. Its 50 to 80 percent step is barely visible, and the 100% landing runs into the footer and site line. Frame 6 puts the subject (one tread and a 5-slab stack) in the bottom quarter, under half a frame of speckled grit. On frame 8 the focal 'not tested' pad is a small chalk rectangle, and QA warns the composition is top-loaded. On frames 3 and 9 the datum is a flat peach band with no metallic response. The 0% stair on frame 3 is cut off by the left edge, and its label sits outside the safe zone (QA warn). On frame 1 the last two dek lines run over the upper treads.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One world (lastLight, key from the left, casts to the right), one material vocabulary (weathering steel stringers, aggregate treads, sawn limestone, one brass datum) and one stair motif that changes state frame by frame. It goes whole-but-gapped (1), definition surface (2), dose walk (3), cliff (4), carcass (5), cut treads (6), rebuilt and short (7), four flights and an empty pad (8), base beside junk (9). The brass datum recurs on 3, 4, 7 and 9 as a second device. Frame 2's plan relief and frame 6's bluer sky sit slightly outside, and frame 4's large mid-tone mass jumps in value against its dark neighbours.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every figure traces to a claim quote or a computation, and every source is primary: the arXiv full text and abstract, plus Texas A&M's own release. The deck keeps the fact-checker's rejections. It prints no 2010 collection year, uses the paper's junk and control definitions rather than the release's, and never says Tu led the study. It falls short of 10 because several phrasings are looser than their sources, though none is false. (1) The caption says 'No Thinking ... showed up in 84% of failures under junk training'. c39 gives 84% for M1 (engagement) junk only and 'over 70%' across all cases. Slide 5 names the set correctly, but the caption drops it. (2) The cover dek's 'trained four language models ... their reasoning skipped steps' gives thought skipping to all four models. The claims don't show which models the failure analysis covered, though the abstract (c38) does say 'models'. (3) Slide 4's headline 'Half junk scored below 80% junk' leaves out the test name and makes a headline of a 1.3-point inversion (59.4 against 60.7) that the paper never interprets. (4) On slide 8, 'Llama3 70B Instruct also fell' doesn't say on what. c58 supports only ARC Challenge, 57.8 to 52.7. (5) Slide 9's 'Testing larger closed models is still needed' is the release's position (c65) printed in the deck's own voice with no attribution. (6) Slide 7 draws the repaired stair at 77.2 minus 17.3. That assumes c47's 'baseline' is the Base column, which c32 supports, and the slide prints no number for it. Lead for the run: art_preflight.json still lists needs_review [9], even though frame 9's review input hashes equal frame_inputs['9']. Confirm panel_ready reads that as stale.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: What happened and who did it are clear: researchers at Texas A&M, UT Austin and Purdue, a COLM 2026 paper, junk defined, a dose response, thought skipping, an incomplete repair. There is no decision, no body, no place beyond the institutions and nothing a Texan can do. The stake for the reader is never stated concretely. Slide 8 honestly says ChatGPT and Gemini were not tested, which removes the link to the tools a reader uses and puts nothing in its place. c64 (doses within a training mix, not a measure of the internet) is in the caption but on no frame. The close is a researcher's general call about data.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover's gapped stair earns the swipe. Frame 2 pays off right away with the definition. The deck turns at frame 6 (the repair), and frame 7 lands the shortfall. Frame 4, the variable-tracking inversion, could be cut without loss and slows the run between the dose (3) and the main failure (5). The close is a quote rather than a consequence, so it lands softly.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register, plain and without hype ('Repaired, still 17.3 points short'), and honest about limits. Some lines read like a machine explaining its own drawing: 'The bare share of the stair is that 84%.' (slide 5) and 'Each landing is its score at one scale.' (slide 3). 'Drawn to illustrate' closes all nine deks. Texas specificity stops at institution names.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: A fresh concept with familiar moves. Per the topics ledger, the deck's whole carrier is a stair: no. 51 on October 15th was 'a granite courthouse stair with a riser for every month', seven days ago. The lastLight world and dark warm-brown palette repeat nos. 54 and 56. The cover opens on one object under the headline, the house default. There is no interior and no counted isotype, unlike no. 55 and no. 56.

one_sentence_fix: Cut frame 4's 1.3-point variable-tracking inversion, which can go without loss and is drawn as three flat beige pier faces in the mid tones. Use the slot for the stake the deck never states: put c63 and c64 (doses within a training mix, not a from-scratch web corpus, not a measure of the internet) on the stair. Then a Texan knows what the finding does and does not mean for the models they use.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Three large flat beige pier faces fill the lower 60% in the grey middle and read as boxes, not a stair walk. The 50 to 80 percent riser is almost invisible, and the 100% landing runs into the footer and texasaidocket.com line.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Pull the camera back and down to a long low oblique, as on frame 3, so the four landings read as lit stair tops with their nosings. Drop the pier faces into shadow by moving the pool onto the 80 percent landing's edge. Raise the framing so the 100% landing sits above the footer band.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The focal 'not tested' pad is a small chalk rectangle at the far right, well under a tenth of the frame. The lower half is empty ground that only carries type (QA top-loaded warn).
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the camera and move it toward the pad, so the empty pad and its chalk outline fill the foreground across about a third of the width, with the four cropped flights rising behind it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: One tread and the 5-slab stack sit in the bottom quarter, under half a frame of speckled grit. The subject is well under a third of the frame, and the sawn face of the 0.8 slab doesn't read.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Drop the eye from 1.38 m to about 0.6 m and move closer, so the stack fills a third to half the frame height. Turn the short top slab so the key rakes its saw face.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The brass datum is a broad flat peach band that reads as painted coping. The 0% stair is cut by the left edge, and its label sits outside the safe zone.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Make the datum a thin inset brass strip with low roughness and metalness, so it catches the key as one bright line. Shift the camera aim right or widen it so the 0% stair and its label sit inside the 80 px margin.
